findings.title: Compilation error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no arguments
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the method defined on the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` (line 160) has the signature `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` and there is no zero-argument overload. This causes a compilation failure.

findings.title: Passkeys conditional UI is disabled on initial login when context.getUser() is null
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, requiring `user != null`. During a normal initial login `context.getUser()` is `null`, so `authenticate()` (line 115) and `challenge()` (line 137) never call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when no user is pre-selected. This completely breaks passkey / conditional UI login whenever the user is not already known (and when `user != null`, it enables conditional passkeys for every user regardless of whether that user has any passkey credentials configured, instead of checking `user == null || webauthnAuth.configuredFor(session, session.getContext().getRealm(), user)`).
